item.content: {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=cognitive+reasoning+agents+incident+reporting+industrial+safety+automated+analysis&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.5220/0007518105830588\", \"title\": [\"Patient Safety Incident Reporting Analysis Based on Integrity and Commitment Team in Inpatient\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.5220/0007518105830588\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2017]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.58837/chula.the.2024.453\", \"title\": [\"Classification dental patient safety incidents and creating a dental incident reporting system model from an academic dental hospital's incident reporting data\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Background: Underreporting of adverse events (AEs) in dentistry hinders patient safety and quality improvement. The Dental Incident Reporting System (DIRS) was developed to address this gap, integrating a comprehensive classification system and user-centered design to enhance reporting accuracy and usability. Methods: This mixed-methods study involved: (1) Developing a classification system using 752 incident reports, validated by experts. (2) Designing DIRS with input from dental professionals and heuristic evaluations by IT experts. (3) Conducting usability testing with 16 participants using the System Usability Scale (SUS) and User Acceptance Test (UAT). Results: The classification system covered 28 categories of dental AEs, aligning with national standards and enabling structured reporting. DIRS achieved a SUS score of 69.69, indicating above-average usability. UAT results showed high ratings for effectiveness (3.15), usefulness (3.15), and satisfaction (3.38). Participant experience had no significant impact on ratings, highlighting DIRS's accessibility across diverse user groups. These results support the broader applicability of DIRS in various dental healthcare settings. Conclusions: DIRS facilitates comprehensive AE documentation and enhances patient safety and risk management. Iterative refinements, guided by expert feedback and usability testing, significantly improved data entry efficiency and report generation.
